reuse.why: All five existing linkers and the new Fintegra one go through the extracted linkBankSyncAccount, and unlinkAccount and the takeover path share clearBankLink; the Fintegra transaction download is still a copy of the Akahu one rather than a shared single-account downloader.

duplication.why: Five copies of the link flow collapse into one and the Akahu/Fintegra balance branch is merged; downloadFintegraTransactions duplicates downloadAkahuTransactions verbatim, and `if (alreadyLinked) clearBankLink` is repeated in both branches of the helper.

placement.why: Link rules (duplicate link, closed account, takeover) live in the single link helper in accounts/app.ts, the download in accounts/sync.ts, and config/types in their usual modules.

scope.why: Covers the five requests; the desktop-client edits only keep the shared provider records type-complete for the new provider.

maintainability.why: One link path with explicit per-provider parameters (bankId, newAccountFields, syncEventTables) is easy to own; fileId is now passed for every provider, which is implicit, and the provider download functions remain copy-per-provider.

bypasses_abstraction.where: Every *-accounts-link handler (GoCardless, SimpleFin, Pluggy, Akahu, Enable Banking, Fintegra) calls linkBankSyncAccount; unlinkAccount uses clearBankLink.

disguised_duplication.where: The only duplicate (downloadFintegraTransactions) is a plain copy of downloadAkahuTransactions, not disguised.

abstraction_drift.where: linkBankSyncAccount in accounts/app.ts gained only replaceExistingLink (step 4). The duplicate-link and closed-account guards apply to every provider, not as special cases, and no link handler bypasses the helper.
